title: Two normalized relative counits have an explicit iterated normal form
statement:
Let $\mathcal C_X,\mathcal C_Y,\mathcal C_B,\mathcal D_X,\mathcal D_Y,\mathcal D_B$ be categories [def-nagata-category]. Composition is functional, $VU=V\circ U$. Functors preserve identities and composition; natural transformations are families of morphisms with commuting naturality squares, and natural isomorphisms have invertible components. Fix functors $F_f:\mathcal C_X\to\mathcal C_Y$, $R_f:\mathcal C_Y\to\mathcal C_X$, $F_g:\mathcal C_Y\to\mathcal C_B$, $R_g:\mathcal C_B\to\mathcal C_Y$, $P_f:\mathcal D_X\to\mathcal D_Y$, $Q_f:\mathcal D_Y\to\mathcal D_X$, $P_g:\mathcal D_Y\to\mathcal D_B$, $Q_g:\mathcal D_B\to\mathcal D_Y$, and $S_i:\mathcal C_i\to\mathcal D_i$. Let $B_f:S_YF_f\xrightarrow{\sim}P_fS_X$ and $B_g:S_BF_g\xrightarrow{\sim}P_gS_Y$ be natural isomorphisms. Fix $H\in\mathcal C_B$, $K\in\mathcal C_X$, put $L=R_fR_gH$, and choose morphisms
$$t:K\to L,\quad e_f:F_fL\to R_gH,\quad e_g:F_gR_gH\to H,$$
$$r:S_YR_gH\to Q_gS_BH,\quad b:S_XL\to Q_fS_YR_gH,$$
$$m_g:P_gQ_gS_BH\to S_BH,\quad m_0:P_fQ_fS_YR_gH\to S_YR_gH,\quad m_1:P_fQ_fQ_gS_BH\to Q_gS_BH.$$
Assume exactly the three equations
$$m_g\circ P_g(r)\circ B_{g,R_gH}=S_B(e_g),\qquad m_0\circ P_f(b)\circ B_{f,L}=S_Y(e_f),$$
$$m_1\circ P_fQ_f(r)=r\circ m_0.$$
Then the following equality holds as maps $P_gP_fS_XK\to S_BH$:
$$m_g\circ P_g(m_1)\circ P_gP_f\bigl(Q_f(r)\circ b\circ S_X(t)\bigr)=S_B\bigl(e_g\circ F_g(e_f)\circ F_gF_f(t)\bigr)\circ B_{g,F_fK}^{-1}\circ P_g(B_{f,K}^{-1}).$$
There is no invertibility assumption on $t,r,b$, no adjunction assumption on $P_h,Q_h$, and no naturality assumption on the chosen $m$ beyond the displayed square. Canonical functor associators are understood.

proof.text:
Write $A$ for the left-hand composite. Expand the image of the three factors using functoriality. Inside $P_g$ the first two consecutive maps are $m_1\circ P_fQ_f(r)$; the third assumed equation replaces these by $r\circ m_0$. Associativity [def-nagata-category] therefore gives
$$A=m_g\circ P_g(r)\circ P_g(m_0)\circ P_gP_f(b)\circ P_gP_fS_X(t).$$

proof.text:
Precompose both sides of the second assumed equation by $B_{f,L}^{-1}$ and cancel $B_{f,L}\circ B_{f,L}^{-1}=\mathrm{id}$, using the category laws [def-nagata-category]. Thus $m_0\circ P_f(b)=S_Y(e_f)\circ B_{f,L}^{-1}$. Apply $P_g$ and substitute into step 1:
$$A=m_g\circ P_g(r)\circ P_gS_Y(e_f)\circ P_g(B_{f,L}^{-1})\circ P_gP_fS_X(t).$$

proof.text:
Precompose both sides of the first assumed equation by $B_{g,R_gH}^{-1}$ and cancel its inverse pair [def-nagata-category]. This gives $m_g\circ P_g(r)=S_B(e_g)\circ B_{g,R_gH}^{-1}$, so
$$A=S_B(e_g)\circ B_{g,R_gH}^{-1}\circ P_gS_Y(e_f)\circ P_g(B_{f,L}^{-1})\circ P_gP_fS_X(t).$$

proof.text:
Naturality of $B_g$ at $e_f:F_fL\to R_gH$ says $P_gS_Y(e_f)\circ B_{g,F_fL}=B_{g,R_gH}\circ S_BF_g(e_f)$. Multiply by the indicated component inverses on the left and right and cancel [def-nagata-category]. Hence $B_{g,R_gH}^{-1}\circ P_gS_Y(e_f)=S_BF_g(e_f)\circ B_{g,F_fL}^{-1}$. Substitute and combine the first two $S_B$ images:
$$A=S_B(e_g\circ F_g(e_f))\circ B_{g,F_fL}^{-1}\circ P_g(B_{f,L}^{-1})\circ P_gP_fS_X(t).$$

proof.text:
Naturality of $B_f$ at $t:K\to L$ gives $P_fS_X(t)\circ B_{f,K}=B_{f,L}\circ S_YF_f(t)$. Multiply by $B_{f,L}^{-1}$ on the left and $B_{f,K}^{-1}$ on the right and cancel [def-nagata-category]. Apply $P_g$ to the resulting equality $B_{f,L}^{-1}\circ P_fS_X(t)=S_YF_f(t)\circ B_{f,K}^{-1}$ and substitute:
$$A=S_B(e_g\circ F_g(e_f))\circ B_{g,F_fL}^{-1}\circ P_gS_YF_f(t)\circ P_g(B_{f,K}^{-1}).$$

source.place: Stacks Tags 0014 (definition-category), 001B (definition-functor), 001I (definition-transformation-functors): agent-written component calculation from the three assumed squares, functoriality and naturality.

proof.text:
Naturality of $B_g$ at $F_f(t):F_fK\to F_fL$ says $P_gS_YF_f(t)\circ B_{g,F_fK}=B_{g,F_fL}\circ S_BF_gF_f(t)$. Compose on the left with $B_{g,F_fL}^{-1}$ and on the right with $B_{g,F_fK}^{-1}$, and cancel the inverse pairs [def-nagata-category]:
$$B_{g,F_fL}^{-1}\circ P_gS_YF_f(t)=S_BF_gF_f(t)\circ B_{g,F_fK}^{-1}.$$
Substitute into step 5 and combine $S_B$ images by functoriality. This gives exactly
$$A=S_B(e_g\circ F_g(e_f)\circ F_gF_f(t))\circ B_{g,F_fK}^{-1}\circ P_g(B_{f,K}^{-1}).$$
